chapter: Parisian Room and Bourbon Street clubs
title: Bawdy tunes and Joe Watkins's dedication at Manny's
summary: Repertoire of mildly suggestive songs at Manny's and Allen's memory of Watkins dedicating a blues.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: What we played: tunes and repertoire in the early days

blocks.x: Uh huh. Uh huh. At Manny's they were playing largely for dancing. And people would make their requests and the band would try to, the band would try to play them. And I don't remember them doing any of their, uh mildly bawdy, uh tunes. Like down on the farm. Uh huh. And uh, oh there, there was a small repertoire of uh, of suggestive, for the time, songs that they used to play. Yeah. At Manny's. And I don't remember ever hearing them at El Morocco but it's not, you know I wasn't there all the time.
I don't remember them ever dedicating uh, never singing uh, some of the pieces. Uh, I can remember Joe Watkins dedicating all the hoars like the way I ride to me. I was at El Morocco or?
I requested it. I think I read about it and Jazz Ways read that it was George's favorite blues or something. Of course, that impressed me.
Yeah. I don't know exactly what he said. He may have said all the girls like the way I drive or something.
I suspect that may have been. Yeah. Or was still sort of a dirty word back then. Yeah.
